What happens each day from pre-op blood tests to Day-7 splint removal?

Most Istanbul rhinoplasty itineraries follow a seven-day cadence: pre-operative labs and in-person surgical mapping on Day 1, general anaesthesia surgery and one hospital night on Day 2, hotel rest from Days 3 to 6, and external splint removal with final surgical review on Day 7 before departure.

According to [Mayo Clinic](https://www.mayoclinic.org/tests-procedures/rhinoplasty/about/pac-20384532), patients typically plan a full week away from routine duties and feel progressively better across those first seven days. As noted by [Cleveland Clinic](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/treatments/11011-rhinoplasty), surgeons apply a small external splint to support the new nasal shape and limit swelling during early healing. Booking a seven-night or eight-night stay gives you margin if your clinic shifts a morning check-up by a few hours.

body.text: When does peak bruising and swelling occur?

Bruising and facial swelling around the eyes and cheeks typically peak between 48 and 72 hours after surgery—meaning Days 3 and 4 of your Istanbul trip—before gradually fading across Days 5 to 7. Full nasal tip refinement continues for months after you return home.

The [American Society of Plastic Surgeons](https://www.plasticsurgery.org/cosmetic-procedures/rhinoplasty/recovery) notes that initial swelling subsides over weeks, while subtle swelling can fluctuate—especially in the mornings—for up to a year. Do not judge your final nasal profile when the cast comes off on Day 7. Expect congestion, mouth breathing, and tight skin across the bridge during the middle of the week, and avoid scheduling tourist excursions on Days 3 and 4.
What hotel room setup (humidifier, elevated pillows, cold packs) helps most?

The most helpful Istanbul hotel room for rhinoplasty recovery sits near your clinic in a quiet street and includes extra firm pillows for a 30-to-45-degree sleeping angle, a cool-mist humidifier to relieve dry mouth from mouth breathing, and mini-fridge freezer access for soft gel cold packs.

When we organize stays through our [medical tourism coordination service](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/services/medical-tourism), we check practical room details before booking rather than relying on star ratings alone.

items: Elevation setup: Request two to three extra firm pillows or bring an inflatable travel wedge so your head stays above heart level while sleeping.
Air moisture: Place a compact cool-mist humidifier beside the bed, as nasal packing or internal splints force mouth breathing overnight.
Cold compress access: Confirm the room has a working mini-fridge or 24-hour ice service for gentle cheek and under-eye cooling (never directly on the splint).
Soft-food proximity: Choose a hotel with room service or nearby cafes offering soups, yogurt, smoothies, and soft proteins that require minimal chewing.
Lift and blackout curtains: Verify elevator access from the lobby and heavy curtains for daytime naps.
Button-up clothing: Pack front-zip hoodies and button-down shirts so nothing brushes over your nose when dressing.

body.text: When is your final surgeon clearance before flying?

Final surgeon clearance happens at your Day-7 post-operative appointment, right after your doctor removes the external cast, inspects incision lines, and applies supportive paper tape. Always book your return flight at least six to eight hours after that appointment—or better yet, on Day 8—to avoid rushing.

Before travel, the [U.S. Embassy in Türkiye](https://tr.usembassy.gov/medical-tourism/) advises verifying provider credentials and carrying comprehensive medical travel insurance. You can also verify whether your chosen facility holds an official authorization certificate through the [Turkish Ministry of Health Health Tourism Department](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html). Ask your surgeon for a signed fit-to-fly letter in English, as airline check-in staff occasionally request written confirmation when passengers travel with visible facial tape or residual bruising.

faq.q: Can I fly home on Day 6 instead of Day 7 after rhinoplasty?
faq.a: Most surgeons schedule external splint removal on Day 6 or Day 7, so leaving earlier risks missing your clinical review. Confirm your exact discharge day with your medical team before locking in non-refundable return tickets.

faq.q: Will cabin pressure damage my nose on the flight home?
faq.a: Commercial cabin pressure changes can temporarily increase sinus congestion and mild swelling, which is why surgeons issue specific nasal spray and hydration guidance. Always follow your licensed medical team's instructions for air travel.

faq.q: Can I explore Istanbul during a 7-day rhinoplasty stay?
faq.a: Light, shaded walks or short private car rides are often possible by Days 5 and 6 if you feel steady and your doctor agrees. Avoid crowded bazaars, heavy sun exposure, and steam rooms or hammams entirely.

faq.q: Should I travel alone or bring a companion?
faq.a: Bringing a companion makes Days 2 through 4 much easier for pharmacy runs, meal pickups, and airport luggage handling. Solo travellers should arrange pre-booked private transfers and hotel room service in advance.

faq.q: How early should I arrive at Istanbul Airport (IST) after cast removal?
faq.a: Plan to reach Istanbul Airport at least three hours before an international departure, and consider pre-booking airport wheelchair or Fast Track assistance to avoid long terminal walks while still tired from surgery.
